title: Major wars in U.S. history, 1754 to 1991
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: Wars are turning points in a nation's story, and their dates are anchors for everything around them: inventions, presidents, new states. This list gives only the dates and who was on each side, so the rest of history has something to hang on.

How to hold it: Chunk by century. The 1700s (two wars, both about who would rule North America), the 1800s (four), and the 1900s (five). Learn one century at a time, then recall the order before the dates. A number hook makes the years stick: 1812 is in the war's own name, and the Civil War's 1861 to 1865 starts with Lincoln's inauguration year. Tie each war to a picture in a memory palace, and come back on day 1, 3, 7 and 21.
This list has 11 items. Answer below, then check — the practice button generates fresh questions from the list itself.
